power.title: Power Analysis Check
report:
::: {.callout-tip title="Learn More" collapse="true"}

Power analyses need to contain the following information to be interpretable: the type of power analysis, the statistical test, the software used, sample size, critical alpha criterion, power level, effect size, and an effect size metric. In addition, it is recommended to make sure the power analysis is reproducible (by sharing the code, or a screenshot, of the power analysis), and to provide good arguments for why the study was designed to detect an effect of this size.

For an a-priori power analysis, where the sample size is determined, reporting all information would look like:

> An a priori power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that for a Cohen's d = 0.5, an alpha level of 0.05, and a desired power level of 80% required at least 64 participants in each group.

For a sensitivity power analysis, this sentence would look like:

> A sensitivity power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that with 64 participants in each group, and an alpha level of 0.05, a desired power level of 80% was reached for an effect size of d = 0.5.

:::

Best practice is to report exact p-values with three decimal places (e.g., *p* = .032) unless *p* values are smaller than 0.001, in which case you can use *p* < .001.

This module sometimes flags false positives when sentences discuss how p-value thresholds were set. It can also miss an imprecise p-value that is reported against a threshold (e.g., "decreased at the *p* < .05 significance threshold").

stat_p_nonsig.report: Meta-scientific research has shown nonsignificant p values are commonly misinterpreted. It is incorrect to infer that there is 'no effect', 'no difference', or that groups are 'the same' after p > 0.05. It is possible that there is a true non-zero effect, but that the study did not detect it. Make sure your inference acknowledges that it is possible that there is a non-zero effect. It is correct to include the effect is 'not significantly' different, although this just restates that p > 0.05. Metacheck does not yet analyze automatically whether sentences which include non-significant p-values are correct, but we recommend manually checking the sentences below for possible misinterpreted non-significant p values. ```{r} #| echo: false # table data -------------------------------------- table <- structure(list(Text = c("P = 0.29", "P=0.60"), Sentence = c("BMI did not differ (mean [SD], 26.6 [6.2] vs 26.4 [5.2]; P = 0.29) (Table 1).", "Risk rose in a graded manner across six STBR ranges, with significant differences between all adjacent ranges except the 2 highest ([0.6-0.7] vs >0.7; P=0.60; Figure 2)." )), row.names = c(NA, -2L), class = c("tbl_df", "tbl", "data.frame" )) # display table ----------------------------------- metacheck::report_table(table, c(0.1, 0.9), 10, FALSE) ``` ::: {.callout-tip title="Learn More" collapse="true"} For metascientific articles demonstrating the rate of misinterpretations of non-significant results is high, see: Aczel B, Palfi B, Szollosi A, Kovacs M, Szaszi B, Szecsi P, Zrubka M, Gronau Q, van den Bergh D, Wagenmakers E (2018). “Quantifying Support for the Null Hypothesis in Psychology: An Empirical Investigation.” Advances in Methods and Practices in Psychological Science, 1(3), 357–366. doi:10.1177/2515245918773742. Murphy S, Merz R, Reimann L, Fernández A (2025). “Nonsignificance misinterpreted as an effect’s absence in psychology: Prevalence and temporal analyses.” Royal Society Open Science, 12(3), 242167. doi:10.1098/rsos.242167. text.text: Does soft tissue signal on bone scintigraphy carry prognostic information in patients without cardiac uptake?

Findings In this cohort study of 8,769 patients without cardiac tracer uptake, a higher soft tissue-tobone ratio was significantly associated with all-cause mortality, major adverse cardiovascular events and heart failure hospitalization after adjustment for 10 risk factors, and in all prespecified subgroups.
The ratio increased significantly across cardiovascular-kidneymetabolic stages.
Meaning Soft tissue-to-bone ratio from routinely acquired bone scans can flag patients with elevated mortality risk and CKM burden at no additional cost.
Extracting risk information from images acquired for other indications is an expanding paradigm in cardiovascular medicine.
Coronary artery calcium on non-gated chest CT is now recommended for routine reporting by cardiovascular imaging societies and an American Heart Association scientific statement 1, 2 .
text.formatted: Coronary artery calcium on non-gated chest CT is now recommended for routine reporting by cardiovascular imaging societies and an American Heart Association scientific statement <ref type="bibr" target="#b0">1,</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b1">2</ref> .

text.text: Such opportunistic markers reach patients who never enter dedicated cardiovascular screening, without additional cost, radiation or acquisition time.
Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome is a prime target for this approach.
It affects most US adults 3, 4 , and the American Heart Association staging framework captures a graded increase in the risk of heart failure and death [5] [6] [7] .
text.formatted: It affects most US adults <ref type="bibr" target="#b2">3,</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b3">4</ref> , and the American Heart Association staging framework captures a graded increase in the risk of heart failure and death <ref type="bibr" target="#b4">[5]</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b5">[6]</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b6">[7]</ref> .

text.text: However, staging relies on categorical thresholds, and its laboratory criteria are often unavailable in routine care.
Substantial heterogeneity also persists within stages 6, 8 .
text.formatted: Substantial heterogeneity also persists within stages <ref type="bibr" target="#b5">6,</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b7">8</ref> .

text.text: A continuous imaging measure of multisystem burden, derived from scans already performed, could flag patients who warrant CKM evaluation and refine risk within stages.
Bone scintigraphy with technetium-99m-labeled bisphosphonates is among the most frequently performed nuclear imaging examinations, used in oncology, orthopedics and rheumatology 9 .
text.formatted: Bone scintigraphy with technetium-99m-labeled bisphosphonates is among the most frequently performed nuclear imaging examinations, used in oncology, orthopedics and rheumatology <ref type="bibr" target="#b8">9</ref> .

text.text: Since the adoption of nonbiopsy diagnostic criteria for transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis, its use in cardiology has grown and large archives have accumulated 10 .
text.formatted: Since the adoption of nonbiopsy diagnostic criteria for transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis, its use in cardiology has grown and large archives have accumulated <ref type="bibr" target="#b9">10</ref> .

text.text: Most scans show no cardiac uptake (Perugini grade 0) and are read as unremarkable, while the soft tissue signal is dismissed as background.
Yet soft tissue tracer retention reflects renal clearance, mineral metabolism and systemic inflammation 9, 11 , each central to CKM pathophysiology.
text.formatted: Yet soft tissue tracer retention reflects renal clearance, mineral metabolism and systemic inflammation <ref type="bibr" target="#b8">9,</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b10">11</ref> , each central to CKM pathophysiology.

text.text: Soft tissue uptake has been linked to amyloid load and mortality in patients with transthyretin amyloidosis 12 , but whether it tracks CKM burden or carries prognostic information in patients without cardiac uptake is unknown.
text.formatted: Soft tissue uptake has been linked to amyloid load and mortality in patients with transthyretin amyloidosis <ref type="bibr" target="#b11">12</ref> , but whether it tracks CKM burden or carries prognostic information in patients without cardiac uptake is unknown.

text.text: We therefore quantified the soft tissue-to-bone ratio (STBR) in 8,769 consecutive patients without cardiac uptake who underwent bone scintigraphy for any indication over a decade.
We tested whether STBR is associated with all-cause mortality, major adverse cardiovascular events and heart failure hospitalization independent of established risk factors and CKM stage.
We also tested whether renal function or cancer explains this association.
Finally, we characterized the clinical traits STBR reflects across 587 diagnoses and measurements and its relationship with CKM stage.

This retrospective single-center cohort study included consecutive patients who underwent 99m Tc-DPD whole-body planar bone scintigraphy for any clinical indication at the Vienna General Hospital between January 2010 and August 2020.
For patients with multiple scans, the first scan was analyzed.
Exclusion criteria were cardiac uptake (Perugini grade ≥1), image quality precluding visual assessment or pathology in both legs precluding measurement (Supplemental Figure S1).
text.formatted: Exclusion criteria were cardiac uptake (Perugini grade ≥1), image quality precluding visual assessment or pathology in both legs precluding measurement (Supplemental Figure <ref type="figure">S1</ref>).

text.text: The ethics committee of the Medical University of Vienna approved the study (2278/2024) and waived informed consent.
The study followed the STROBE reporting guideline.
Race and ethnicity are not recorded in the institutional records and were therefore not analyzed.
Demographic, laboratory, echocardiographic and cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) data were extracted from institutional electronic health records.
Comorbidities were defined by 3-character ICD-10 codes from medical reports as well as admission and discharge records of the Vienna Health Network, comprising 7 major public hospitals.
Vital status was obtained from the national death registry.
The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality.
Secondary endpoints were major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE; cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction or nonfatal stroke) and heart failure hospitalization.
Follow-up started at the scan date.

Planar anterior and posterior whole-body images were acquired approximately 2.5 hours after intravenous injection of approximately 650 MBq 99m Tc-DPD on 1 of 5 dual-head gamma cameras using standardized institutional protocols.
Two trained observers blinded to outcomes placed 16-mm circular regions of interest over the mid-diaphyseal femur and tibia of the right leg, each paired with an adjacent soft tissue region.
The left leg was used when the right was not assessable (Supplemental Figures S2 and S3).
text.formatted: The left leg was used when the right was not assessable (Supplemental Figures <ref type="figure">S2</ref> and <ref type="figure">S3</ref>).

text.text: STBR was calculated as the ratio of mean soft tissue to mean bone counts per pixel, averaged across the upper and lower leg.
Both observers independently read 200 randomly selected scans to assess inter-reader agreement.
STBR was analyzed continuously and dichotomized at 0.5.
To characterize the clinical correlates of STBR, we performed an imaging-phenotype association (IPA) analysis analogous to phenome-and genome-wide association studies 13, 14.

Because CKM-defining variables were frequently missing, 4 analytic strategies were specified before the CKM analysis.

These were a best-evidence-available approach as the primary analysis, a completecase analysis, multiple imputation by chained equations with 20 imputations and the bestevidence-available approach restricted to patients without cancer.
The association between STBR and CKM stage was quantified by Spearman correlation, pooled across imputations using Fisher z transformation under Rubin rules.
Continuous variables are reported as mean (SD) or median (IQR) and were compared using Welch t-tests, Mann-Whitney U tests, Chi-square or Fisher exact tests.

Cox proportional hazards models were fitted unadjusted and adjusted for 10 established risk factors, namely age, sex, BMI, renal insufficiency, cancer, diabetes, hypertension, coronary artery disease, atrial fibrillation and liver disease.
STBR was modeled dichotomized, per 1-SD increase and with restricted cubic splines and 4 knots.
The proportional hazards assumption was assessed using scaled Schoenfeld residuals.

Inter-reader agreement was assessed using the intraclass correlation coefficient and Bland-Altman analysis.

It was inversely associated with total and LDL cholesterol, hemoglobin and hematocrit.

In 8,769 consecutive patients without cardiac uptake on bone scintigraphy, soft tissue signal routinely dismissed as background was associated with all-cause mortality, MACE and heart failure hospitalization independent of 10 established risk factors.
Risk increased in a graded manner with STBR.
The association was not explained by renal function, cancer or any other single comorbidity.
STBR mapped predominantly to cardiovascular, renal and metabolic traits, increased across CKM stages and added prognostic information beyond CKM stage.
These findings identify STBR as an opportunistic marker of systemic cardiovascular risk that can be derived from scans already performed at most hospitals.
Several observations argue against STBR being a surrogate of a known risk factor.

Renal clearance is the principal excretion route of bisphosphonate tracers 9 , yet STBR remained prognostic in patients without renal insufficiency and outperformed eGFR for mortality discrimination when combined with age.
text.formatted: Renal clearance is the principal excretion route of bisphosphonate tracers <ref type="bibr" target="#b8">9</ref> , yet STBR remained prognostic in patients without renal insufficiency and outperformed eGFR for mortality discrimination when combined with age.

text.text: The association was substantially stronger in patients without cancer, arguing against STBR being a purely cancer-associated marker.
BMI did not differ by STBR category, making soft tissue thickness an unlikely explanation.
The association was also consistent across sex, age and referral indication.
The biological basis of STBR is likely multifactorial.

Bisphosphonate tracers bind hydroxyapatite-like calcium deposits 15, 16 , and dysregulated mineral metabolism across the CKM spectrum promotes ectopic vascular and soft tissue calcification [17] [18] [19] .

text.text: The IPA supports a composite signal, with associations spanning cardiac strain (NT-proBNP, chamber dimensions), inflammation (CRP), renal function and hepatic function.

Inverse associations with cholesterol and hemoglobin are consistent with the pattern seen in advanced cardiometabolic disease, in which low cholesterol marks frailty rather than favorable risk 20, 21 .

text.text: Dedicated mechanistic studies are needed to separate these contributions.
These findings are relevant to CKM risk assessment.
CKM stage predicts heart failure and death 6, 7 , but staging is categorical and depends on laboratory data that are often missing, as illustrated by unavailable eGFR in 45% of our cohort.

text.text: STBR increased across stages in all four analytic strategies and stratified mortality within every stage, including stage 0, without effect modification.
A continuous imaging index could therefore complement staging by not only identifying patients for CKM evaluation but also for refining risk within stages.
STBR extends the paradigm of opportunistic cardiovascular imaging.
Coronary artery calcium on non-gated chest CT predicts cardiovascular and all-cause mortality 22, 23 and is now recommended for routine reporting 1, 2 .

text.text: STBR can be annotated in seconds on every routine medical image viewer.
Because bone scintigraphy is not part of CKM evaluation, its value lies in opportunistic use.

STBR derived from scans acquired for other indications could identify patients with unrecognized CKM burden who may benefit from targeted evaluation of blood pressure, glycemia, lipids, kidney function and albuminuria 5, 25 .

text.text: In patients with an available scan, STBR may also refine risk within CKM stages and help prioritize intensified management of modifiable risk factors, although whether STBR-guided management improves outcomes requires prospective evaluation.
Automated quantification would enable the scalable application to existing archives.
Prior quantitative analyses of bone scintigraphy treated soft tissue activity as a denominator for cardiac uptake rather than as a signal of interest 26 .

text.text: In wild-type transthyretin amyloidosis, Tingen et al. linked soft tissue uptake to subcutaneous amyloid load and mortality 12 .
text.formatted: In wild-type transthyretin amyloidosis, Tingen et al. linked soft tissue uptake to subcutaneous amyloid load and mortality <ref type="bibr" target="#b11">12</ref> .

text.text: Because these patients typically have advanced age, heart failure, atrial fibrillation and chronic kidney disease, soft tissue uptake in amyloidosis may reflect extracardiac amyloid deposition, comorbid CKM burden or both.
Our results show that the soft tissue signal is also prognostic in patients without cardiac uptake but does not distinguish between these mechanisms in patients with amyloidosis.
This study has limitations.
First, it was a single-center retrospective study and external validation is required.
Second, CKM staging was adapted to available data, using eGFR without albuminuria and BMI without waist circumference.
To account for this, we applied four analytic strategies, which yielded concordant gradients.
Third, planar imaging is subject to attenuation and overlap, and SPECT could enable volumetric quantification.
Fourth, regions of interest were placed manually, although inter-reader agreement was excellent.
Fifth, most patients were referred for oncologic indications, reflecting the population undergoing bone scintigraphy.
Cancer treatment data were unavailable.
Sixth, only 99m Tc-DPD was studied.
Generalization to other bisphosphonate tracers requires validation.
Bone scintigraphy has been widely available and routinely performed for decades, yet the soft tissue signal on scans without cardiac uptake has been disregarded as background.
In 8,769 such patients, the soft tissue-to-bone ratio was independently associated with all-cause 334 mortality, major adverse cardiovascular events and heart failure hospitalization.
The 335 association held in women and men, in younger and older patients and in patients with and 336 without cancer or renal insufficiency.
STBR also tracked cumulative cardiovascular-kidney-337 metabolic burden.
Because STBR can be derived from routinely acquired scans without 338 additional imaging, radiation or cost, it may enable opportunistic detection and risk 339 stratification.
